answer: Agents earn influence only after completing tasks that counterparties independently verify, with each verification tied to a distinct, stake-bearing account and capped so one account cannot endorse an entire network. A prism of cross-checks makes a spiral of disposable identities ineffective: new accounts lack verified history, while colluding accounts expose their shared stake to slashing when audits find fabricated work. The attacker must therefore fund many identities and risk losing that capital, not merely mint usernames; umber marks the costly shadow of each false claim.
